Commercial Package Unit In San Diego

Keep your building comfortable, efficient, and ready for business with a commercial packaged system that does the heavy lifting without taking up valuable indoor space. Sky Clean Air installs, repairs, and maintains every part of your commercial package unit, and we do it with speed and clear communication. Need help today? Call {{phone}} or visit skycleanair.com.

From rooftop units keeping a Mission Valley office cool, to packaged systems serving a Point Loma retail center near the coast, we know San Diego buildings and we know what your equipment goes through. Salt air, long cooling seasons, wildfire smoke days, and permit rules in different neighborhoods all play a part. We handle it so you can focus on running your business.

What is a Commercial Package Unit and why it fits San Diego properties

A commercial package unit combines all the heating, cooling, and ventilation parts in one cabinet. Most units sit on the roof. That frees up space indoors and keeps noise out of tenant areas. Learn more about typical rooftop units. In San Diego, this setup is popular for

  • Strip malls and quick service restaurants
  • Medical offices and professional suites
  • Warehouses and light industrial spaces
  • Schools, gyms, and community centers
  • Downtown mixed use buildings with tight footprints

San Diego’s climate stays mild for much of the year, but buildings still need reliable cooling during warm spells and solid ventilation all year. Many sites near the ocean see early coil corrosion. Inland zones see more dust. A smart package unit choice and steady care help avoid breakdowns and high bills. Consider regular commercial HVAC maintenance to stay ahead.

Services we provide for Commercial Package Unit In San Diego

We offer same day help for many calls, plus planned installs and upgrades. Whether you need emergency repair, a new unit, or a quarterly maintenance plan, Sky Clean Air has you covered. Explore our commercial emergency HVAC services when time is critical.

New installation and replacement

Thinking about replacing an old rooftop unit that keeps tripping off. We make installation simple and safe from start to finish. See our commercial HVAC installation and commercial HVAC replacement services.

Our process for installs and change outs

  • Site visit and load review We check roof access, curb size, electrical service, gas lines if present, and duct connections. We look at your space use, hours, people count, and any internal heat loads from cooking or equipment. This prevents sizing mistakes that cause hot and cold spots.
  • Options and clear pricing You receive options with efficiency ratings, tonnage, heating type, and control choices. We explain what each choice means for energy use, comfort, and code compliance with California Title 24.
  • Permits and scheduling We pull the required permit with the City of San Diego or your local jurisdiction, coordinate any inspections, and set a crane date if needed. Downtown lifts may need traffic control. We handle it.
  • Removal and curb work We remove the old unit, adapt the curb if the footprint differs, and seal roof penetrations to keep water out. We protect landscaping, vehicles, and pedestrians during the lift.
  • Connections and start up Our team connects power, gas or heat pump lines, controls, and fresh air ducts. We test airflow, heat, cooling, and economizer operation. You receive a start up report and photos.
  • Walkthrough and training We show your building or facilities staff how to use the thermostat or BAS interface and how to replace filters on schedule.

Replacement is a good time to add energy saving features like demand control ventilation, smart controls, and higher efficiency motors. Ask us what fits your building.

Fast repair on all major brands

Is the AC running but the rooms still feel stuffy. Hear a rattle on the roof that sounds like a loose toolbox. Call {{phone}} for same day repair in most San Diego areas. Learn more about commercial HVAC repair.

Common issues we fix

  • No cooling or weak airflow
  • Unit short cycles or trips the breaker
  • Blower motor failure or worn belts
  • Dirty coils leading to poor heat transfer
  • Economizer damper stuck open or closed
  • Thermostat or sensor faults
  • Refrigerant leaks or low charge
  • Gas heat not firing, ignition problems
  • Drain clogs and water leaks
  • Odd smells after long off cycles

We stock common parts and have quick access to others. If you need a temporary solution to keep tenants comfortable while waiting for a special order part, we can often stage fans or adjust ventilation to buy time.

Preventive maintenance that actually prevents problems

A well kept commercial package unit lasts longer and costs less to run. In San Diego, a quarterly plan works well for most sites. Coastal properties may need more frequent coil cleaning due to salt spray. Ask about commercial HVAC maintenance and commercial AC cleaning.

Typical maintenance tasks we perform

  • Replace or clean filters to the right MERV rating
  • Inspect and adjust belts, pulleys, and bearings
  • Clean condenser and evaporator coils
  • Rinse drain pans and clear condensate lines
  • Test economizer, actuators, and minimum outside air
  • Check refrigerant pressures, superheat, and subcooling
  • Test heat section, burners, gas pressure, and safeties
  • Tighten electrical connections and test capacitors
  • Verify airflow, temperature split, and static pressure
  • Review control settings and schedules

We provide an easy to read report after each visit, with photos and a plan for any needed repairs. No surprises and no pushy add ons.

Energy saving upgrades that pay you back

Want to lower your SDG&E bill without sacrificing comfort. Ask about upgrades that reduce run time and improve control. We can pair this with airflow balancing and duct sealing for better results.

Smart upgrades for commercial packaged systems

  • Premium coil cleaning and protective coating for coastal buildings
  • Variable frequency drives on supply or return fans where suitable
  • ECM motors for better efficiency and quieter operation
  • Economizer tune up and sensor replacement
  • Demand control ventilation using CO2 sensors
  • Smart thermostats or BAS integration with proper scheduling
  • High efficiency filters with low pressure drop
  • Duct sealing and repairs to cut leakage
  • UV C lamps on coils to reduce biofilm and keep coils clean

We can also advise on rebate programs and code rules that may affect your choices.

Signs your unit needs attention

Catching issues early prevents bigger bills and downtime. Do any of these sound familiar.

  • Rising energy costs without a change in hours or occupancy
  • Hot and cold spots across suites or floors
  • Longer run times to reach setpoint
  • Loud rattles, squeals, or fan noise on startup
  • Musty or burnt smells at first cycle
  • Frequent service calls for the same issue
  • Water around roof drains or stains below
  • Tenants propping doors open to get fresh air

If you checked two or more, your system may need service soon. Call {{phone}} for a quick assessment.

Choosing the right Commercial Package Unit for your property

A good unit matches the space, usage, and budget. Are you weighing a simple replacement or a more efficient upgrade. We can help you pick what fits. We can begin with a thorough commercial HVAC inspection.

Factors we review with you

  • Capacity and airflow Tonnage that matches your load, with enough static pressure for your duct system.
  • Heating type Gas heat, electric heat, or heat pump based on utility rates, roof gas access, and comfort goals.
  • Efficiency ratings EER and IEER matter in San Diego because much of the year is part load. Better IEER often lowers real bills.
  • Ventilation requirements Meet fresh air rules while keeping control over humidity and energy. That means a working economizer and sensors that make sense for your zone.
  • Controls From simple programmable stats to BACnet connections. We set up schedules, lockouts, and alarms you can actually use. See our commercial thermostat installation and commercial thermostat programming.
  • Noise and neighbors Rooftop units near residential areas need quiet operation. Fan choices and vibration pads help.
  • Footprint and curb Replacements may need a curb adapter. We check roof structure and drainage to avoid leaks.
  • Power and gas Verify voltage, phase, and gas piping before replacement day to avoid delays.
  • Location Buildings near the coast may need corrosion resistant parts. Inland sites may benefit from extra filtration and easy access for filter changes during dust season.

Indoor air quality and ventilation that matches San Diego days

Your packaged unit does more than heat and cool. It also brings in outside air. On some days, that air needs extra care.

  • Wildfire smoke days We can place a higher MERV filter strategy for those periods and adjust economizers to limit smoke entry.
  • Coastal moisture Early morning fog can load coils with moisture. Clean coils shed water better, which helps airflow and keeps microbial growth down.
  • Pollen and dust season Filter upgrades and regular changes keep occupants more comfortable and protect your coils.
  • Ventilation balance Too little fresh air leads to stuffy rooms. Too much raises bills. We test and set the right minimum and verify operation.

As an air duct cleaning service provider, Sky Clean Air also inspects and cleans connected ductwork. Clean ducts lower static pressure and can boost delivered airflow. That helps your commercial package unit perform better without working harder. Ask about commercial air duct cleaning and commercial duct leakage testing.

Have a building near the water. We can add coil coatings and hardware that stand up better to salt air. Have a tight rooftop downtown. We schedule lifts early and keep noise to a minimum.

Our clear process from first call to final check

You want less downtime and no confusion. Here is how we keep projects moving.

Frequently serviced components on commercial packaged systems

We troubleshoot and repair all parts of your packaged unit.

  • Compressors and contactors
  • Condenser and evaporator coils
  • Blower motors and VFDs
  • Belts, pulleys, and bearings
  • Economizers, actuators, and dampers
  • Ignition systems, burners, and heat exchangers
  • Expansion valves and refrigerant piping
  • Control boards, sensors, and thermostats
  • Power distribution and disconnects
  • Condensate pans, traps, and drains

Maintenance checklist for your team

Your staff can help keep things smooth between our visits. Here are simple checks that do not require opening panels.

Monthly quick checks

  • Replace filters on the schedule we set
  • Listen for new noises at startup and shutdown
  • Look for standing water near roof drains
  • Check thermostats for correct date and time
  • Keep the outdoor area around the unit free of debris
  • Log any hot or cold complaints by room or suite

If you notice anything odd, call us. Early calls prevent bigger repairs and longer downtime. Reach out through our contact page for quick scheduling.

Energy, efficiency, and controls that make sense

Not sure if you should switch to a heat pump or stay with gas heat. Wondering if a smart thermostat will really help. We match choices to real usage. Ask about commercial HVAC zoning setup and commercial HVAC control setup to improve comfort and savings.

  • Heat type Gas heat is common and can be cost effective where gas rates are stable. Heat pumps can help where cooling runs most of the year and the building has good duct sealing. Dual fuel can provide flexibility.
  • Controls Smart thermostats and BAS tie ins allow scheduling, remote view, and alarms. We set moderate temperature ranges that reduce energy use and limit tenant tug of war.
  • Economizers On cool dry days in San Diego, the economizer can cool your building with outside air. When smoke or high humidity hits, we limit outside air to protect comfort and indoor air quality.
  • Filtration We select filters that meet indoor air needs without choking the system. MERV 8 to 13 covers many sites. We balance clean air with airflow and energy use.
  • VFDs and ECMs Variable speed control can reduce fan energy use during part load. We confirm duct static and motor compatibility before we recommend a change.

Want a simple energy checkup with your next maintenance visit. Ask us to include it. You will get practical steps you can act on right away.

What affects cost and timelines

Transparent pricing helps you plan. Here is what can raise or lower project cost.

  • Tonnage and efficiency rating of the unit
  • Access and crane needs, plus street restrictions
  • Curb adapter or roof reinforcement
  • Duct modifications or sealing work
  • Control upgrades or BAS integration
  • Gas line or electrical upgrades
  • Permit fees and required inspections
  • Coastal coatings or special order parts

You will never guess what a line item means. We explain each part of the quote and show where you can save now or over time.

Real San Diego scenarios we solve

North Park retail suite

A small clothing shop had a unit that kept short cycling at midday. We found clogged filters and a stuck economizer. A simple fix and better filter schedule solved the problem and lowered the bill.

Sorrento Valley office

An older rooftop unit ran loud and bothered nearby tenants. We replaced worn bearings, balanced the fan, and added vibration pads. Noise dropped and the unit ran smoother.

Pacific Beach restaurant

Grease laden air was coating the rooftop coil. We set up a coil maintenance plan and added a protective coating. The unit now holds temp on busy nights without constant runs.

Chula Vista warehouse

Staff complained about warm zones near the loading area. We found duct leakage and a broken damper. Sealing and damper repairs improved airflow. The manager reported fewer hot spot complaints. We often pair this with commercial duct balancing.

La Jolla medical office

They needed better filtration during smoke days. We upgraded to MERV 13 filters, tuned the economizer control, and set a filter change schedule. Air quality improved and the system stayed within safe pressure.

What about refrigerants

Many older units use refrigerants that are being phased out. Newer systems use options with better performance and lower environmental impact. We help you pick a unit that meets current rules and is serviceable for years ahead. During service, we recover and handle refrigerant responsibly.

Safety and building rules

We follow site rules and keep your building safe during work. That includes barricades during crane lifts, roof protection, and coordination with security. We test gas heat for safe operation and confirm ventilation settings. Your people and your property come first.

The simple benefit of clean ducts with a new packaged unit

Replacing a rooftop unit but keeping old ducts that leak and carry dust is like putting new tires on a car with bent wheels. We offer duct inspection and cleaning so your new commercial package unit does not fight against dirty or leaky paths. The result is better airflow, less strain, and cleaner indoor air.
